name: Bakery department customer floor east of the back-of-house wall (customer): the five drawn display tables [315.7,261.3,350.5,270.2], [316.1,290.1,351,298.3], [315.3,319.8,350.1,328], [315.7,351.2,350.5,359.4], [319.1,380.9,342.8,387.4] with the 19-pt walkway west of them (x=296-315, against the wall) and the 24-pt north-south walkway east of them (x=351-375, against the Beer/Wine gondola at x=375). None of these is a counter — they are open self-service tables, so the BAKERY title (332.5,309.9) printed among them is a department name on the shopping floor, not a label inside a service enclosure, and its VERIFY is a false positive. The auto BAKERY seal disk (r=130 about that title, bridge 12) reached through the staff door at x=294.8-296.4 and merged 78 m2 of this floor — the top two tables and the aisle around them, y=238..326 — into the same pocket as the back-of-house wedge, which the title then condemned as staff. The wedge is now sealed on its own drawn wall (exclusions.json), so this rect only has to restore the customer half; it can restore nothing west of that wall because exclusions are removed from the grid before inclusions are applied

Market floor around the Seafood title (customer): the open floor between the freestanding diagonal seafood case [approx x=335-367, y=193-240] and the Market island gondola [377.6,166.4,479.7,188] to its north, where the SEAFOOD title (361.8,194.1) is printed. Nothing here is drawn as an enclosure — the case stands free with walkable floor on all four sides, exactly the shape 658 records for its Deli title ('no staff enclosure exists on this side'). This store's actual seafood SERVICE case is the scalloped wall run drawn on the back-of-house wall at x=300-335 / y=133-176, and its staff side is the sealed wedge behind that wall, so the 71%-walkable VERIFY at the title is customer space

Restrooms vestibule off the front alley (customer): the 37.7 x 76 pt (3.5 x 7 m) walled bay drawn between the wall x=441.6 (y=570..663), the wall x=479.3 (y=586.7..663), the wall y=586.7 (x=457.7..479.3) and the store's front wall y=663, entered through the 16-pt gap its north-west corner leaves at x=441.6..457.7 under the RESTROOMS title (468.6,578.2). The only thing drawn inside it is the printed restroom pictogram — the same kind of sign glyph as the wheelchair/exit sign beside it — which extract.py captures as fixture polys [445.2,600,472.4,639.8] and so fences the bay's floor into a 3-pt-wide ring. What actually sealed the bay was the auto DELI disk (r=130 about the Deli title at 333.4,580.6, 10 m away): its rim bridged the 16-pt mouth and culled the whole 11 m2 bay as a dead crevice. Verified by rebuilding with that one disk removed — the bay is then free and entrance-reachable with no other change, which is the definition of a seal-rim over-reach, not a drawn enclosure

Aisle 13 corridor at the 'Kitchen Gadgets' shelf label (customer): the 19.5-pt corridor between gondolas [806.6,221.5,819.3,513.7] and [838.8,223.3,851.4,513.6], badged AISLE 13 at (826.9,213.3). The extracted KITCHEN anchor (823.7,498) is the bottom of the printed product-category column 'Kitchen Gadgets / Cookware / Bakeware / Appliances' (x=818-829, y=260-511), not a service kitchen — the same false anchor stores 24, 388, 658, 660, 790 and 811 all record. seal_zones.json therefore drops its auto disk, and this rect suppresses the VERIFY that the label would otherwise raise standing in an ordinary shopping aisle
